consistencyRules.message: Item 1a = 3 (coma): NINDS instructions automatically score item 8 (sensory) as 2.
Item 1a = 3 (coma): NINDS instructions automatically score item 9 (language) as 3.
Item 9 = 3 is used only if the patient is mute and follows no one-step commands, but item 1c records at least one command performed.
No movement in all four limbs: NINDS instructions score ataxia as absent in a paralysed patient.

name: NIH Stroke Scale

version.label: NINDS NIH Stroke Scale (2024 update), 15 items
version.detail: Items 1a–11 as defined by NINDS (updated February 2024). Total 0–42. The language stimulus pictures, naming sheet and reading lists are not reproduced. Optional add-on items (e.g. distal motor function) are not part of the scale total and are not included.

purpose: Standardised quantification of selected neurological deficits after stroke, for assessment, monitoring and communication.
intendedPopulation: Adults with suspected or confirmed acute stroke, examined by a clinician trained in the NIHSS.

calculatorNotice.title: Not a complete neurological examination
calculatorNotice.message: NIHSS scores 15 selected items. Disabling deficits such as gait or truncal ataxia, vertigo, dysphagia, isolated hand weakness and cognitive impairment are not captured. A low score, including 0, does not exclude stroke.

inputDefinitions.label: 1a. Level of consciousness
inputDefinitions.help: A response must be chosen even if evaluation is limited (e.g. endotracheal tube, language barrier). Score 3 only if no movement other than reflexive posturing to noxious stimulation.

options.label: Not alert; arousable by minor stimulation
options.detail: To obey, answer or respond.

options.label: Not alert; requires repeated stimulation
options.detail: Or obtunded, requiring strong or painful stimulation to make movements (not stereotyped).

options.label: Reflex responses only, or totally unresponsive
options.detail: Reflex motor or autonomic effects only, or flaccid and areflexic.

inputDefinitions.label: 1b. LOC questions
inputDefinitions.help: Ask the month and the patient's age; grade only the initial answer, with no partial credit. Aphasic or stuporous patients who do not comprehend score 2. Patients unable to speak for reasons other than aphasia (e.g. intubation) score 1.

inputDefinitions.label: 1c. LOC commands
inputDefinitions.help: Open and close the eyes; grip and release the non-paretic hand. Credit an unequivocal attempt limited by weakness. Pantomime if no response. Only the first attempt is scored.

inputDefinitions.label: 2. Best gaze
inputDefinitions.help: Horizontal eye movements only; voluntary or oculocephalic, no caloric testing. Conjugate deviation overcome by voluntary or reflexive activity, or an isolated CN III, IV or VI paresis, scores 1.

options.label: Partial gaze palsy
options.detail: Gaze abnormal in one or both eyes; no forced deviation or total gaze paresis.

options.label: Forced deviation or total gaze paresis
options.detail: Not overcome by the oculocephalic manoeuvre.

inputDefinitions.label: 3. Visual
inputDefinitions.help: Confrontation testing of upper and lower quadrants. Score 1 only for clear-cut asymmetry, including quadrantanopia. Blind from any cause scores 3.

options.label: Bilateral hemianopia
options.detail: Blind, including cortical blindness.

options.label: Minor paralysis
options.detail: Flattened nasolabial fold, asymmetry on smiling.

options.label: Partial paralysis
options.detail: Total or near-total paralysis of the lower face.

options.label: Complete paralysis of one or both sides
options.detail: No facial movement in upper and lower face.

inputDefinitions.label: 5a. Motor arm, left
inputDefinitions.help: Position the arm at 90° (sitting) or 45° (supine). Drift is scored if it falls before 10 seconds. Begin with the non-paretic limb. UN only for amputation or joint fusion at the shoulder.

notTestable.label: Untestable (UN)
notTestable.description: Only for amputation or joint fusion; record the reason.

options.label: No drift
options.detail: Holds position for the full 10 seconds.

options.label: Drift
options.detail: Drifts down before 10 seconds; does not hit the bed or other support.

options.label: Some effort against gravity
options.detail: Cannot get to or maintain position; falls to bed, but some effort against gravity.

options.label: No effort against gravity
options.detail: Limb falls.

inputDefinitions.label: 5b. Motor arm, right
inputDefinitions.help: Position the arm at 90° (sitting) or 45° (supine). Drift is scored if it falls before 10 seconds. Begin with the non-paretic limb. UN only for amputation or joint fusion at the shoulder.

notTestable.label: Untestable (UN)
notTestable.description: Only for amputation or joint fusion; record the reason.

options.label: No drift
options.detail: Holds position for the full 10 seconds.

options.label: Drift
options.detail: Drifts down before 10 seconds; does not hit the bed or other support.

options.label: Some effort against gravity
options.detail: Cannot get to or maintain position; falls to bed, but some effort against gravity.

options.label: No effort against gravity
options.detail: Limb falls.

inputDefinitions.label: 6a. Motor leg, left
inputDefinitions.help: Position the leg at 30° (always supine). Drift is scored if it falls before 5 seconds. Begin with the non-paretic limb. UN only for amputation or joint fusion at the hip.

notTestable.label: Untestable (UN)
notTestable.description: Only for amputation or joint fusion; record the reason.

options.label: No drift
options.detail: Holds position for the full 5 seconds.

options.label: Drift
options.detail: Drifts down before 5 seconds; does not hit the bed or other support.

options.label: Some effort against gravity
options.detail: Cannot get to or maintain position; falls to bed, but some effort against gravity.

options.label: No effort against gravity
options.detail: Limb falls.

inputDefinitions.label: 6b. Motor leg, right
inputDefinitions.help: Position the leg at 30° (always supine). Drift is scored if it falls before 5 seconds. Begin with the non-paretic limb. UN only for amputation or joint fusion at the hip.

notTestable.label: Untestable (UN)
notTestable.description: Only for amputation or joint fusion; record the reason.

options.label: No drift
options.detail: Holds position for the full 5 seconds.

options.label: Drift
options.detail: Drifts down before 5 seconds; does not hit the bed or other support.

options.label: Some effort against gravity
options.detail: Cannot get to or maintain position; falls to bed, but some effort against gravity.

options.label: No effort against gravity
options.detail: Limb falls.

inputDefinitions.label: 7. Limb ataxia
inputDefinitions.help: Finger-nose-finger and heel-shin on both sides, eyes open. Scored only if out of proportion to weakness. Ataxia is absent in a patient who cannot understand or is paralysed.

notTestable.label: Untestable (UN)
notTestable.description: Only for amputation or joint fusion; record the reason.

inputDefinitions.label: 8. Sensory
inputDefinitions.help: Pinprick, or withdrawal in the obtunded or aphasic patient. Only stroke-related loss counts. Bilateral loss from brainstem stroke scores 2; unresponsive and quadriplegic scores 2; coma (1a = 3) scores 2.

options.label: Mild-to-moderate sensory loss
options.detail: Pinprick less sharp or dull, or loss of superficial pain but aware of being touched.

options.label: Severe or total sensory loss
options.detail: Not aware of being touched in face, arm and leg.

inputDefinitions.label: 9. Best language
inputDefinitions.help: Uses the NINDS picture, naming and reading materials (not reproduced here). Coma (1a = 3) scores 3. Score 3 only if the patient is mute and follows no one-step commands.

options.label: Mild-to-moderate aphasia
options.detail: Some loss of fluency or comprehension; examiner can still identify the material from the response.

options.label: Severe aphasia
options.detail: Fragmentary expression; examiner cannot identify the material from the response.

options.label: Mute, global aphasia
options.detail: No usable speech or auditory comprehension.

inputDefinitions.label: 10. Dysarthria
inputDefinitions.help: Obtain an adequate speech sample (NINDS word list, not reproduced). UN only if intubated or another physical barrier to producing speech.

notTestable.label: Untestable (UN)
notTestable.description: Only if intubated or another physical barrier to speech; record the reason.

options.label: Mild-to-moderate dysarthria
options.detail: Slurs at least some words; at worst understood with some difficulty.

options.label: Severe dysarthria
options.detail: Unintelligible out of proportion to any dysphasia, or mute/anarthric.

inputDefinitions.label: 11. Extinction and inattention
inputDefinitions.help: Never untestable. Severe visual loss with normal cutaneous stimuli scores normal; an aphasic patient who attends to both sides scores normal.

options.label: Inattention or extinction in one modality
options.detail: Visual, tactile, auditory, spatial or personal.

options.label: Profound hemi-inattention or extinction to more than one modality
options.detail: Does not recognise own hand, or orients to only one side of space.

resultStates.label: No measurable deficit
resultStates.summary: No measurable deficit on the NIHSS at the time of assessment.
resultStates.detail: This does not exclude stroke: deficits outside the scale's 15 items are not captured.

resultStates.label: NIHSS {total}
resultStates.summary: Higher scores indicate more measured neurological deficit.
resultStates.detail: NINDS defines no severity categories, and bands used in studies differ. Interpret the item profile and trend with imaging and the full examination.

clinicalContext.text: Quantifies 15 selected neurological deficits after stroke.
Used for serial monitoring; change between assessments by trained examiners is often more informative than one value.
Provides a common language between emergency, stroke and research teams.

clinicalInsights.text: Report the total with the item breakdown; the same total can reflect very different deficits.
Deficits outside the scale, such as gait or truncal ataxia, vertigo, nystagmus or dysphagia, can be present with a score of 0.
Language-dependent items contribute to this total. For similar lesion volume, left-hemisphere strokes tend to score higher than right-hemisphere strokes.
Inattention or extinction is present. Neglect may be under-weighted relative to its functional impact.
Low scores can accompany disabling deficits, particularly in posterior circulation stroke.

limitations.text: Not a complete neurological examination: gait and truncal ataxia, vertigo, nystagmus, dysphagia, isolated distal hand weakness and cognition are not scored.
Under-represents posterior circulation stroke; a score of 0 does not exclude stroke.

limitations: Language-weighted: right-hemisphere strokes may score lower than left-hemisphere strokes of similar size.
The total does not show which deficits are disabling for this patient.
Reliability depends on trained, certified examiners following the item rules.

limitations.text: {nt_count} item(s) untestable and contributing no points: the total may underestimate the deficit.
limitations.guideText: Untestable (UN) items contribute no points, so the total may underestimate the deficit.

confounders.effect: Limits consciousness, language and dysarthria items.
Old deficits are scored unless documented separately.
Affects comprehension of commands and questions (items 1b, 1c).
Can affect visual field, command and language items.
Motor or ataxia items recorded as UN.
Can produce scorable deficits without stroke.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Whether the deficit is caused by stroke or a mimic.
Stroke mechanism, vessel occlusion or infarct size.
The full neurological picture, including posterior circulation signs and cognition.
commonErrors: Coaching the patient, or scoring a later rather than the first attempt (1b, 1c).
Going back to change earlier item scores.
Scoring ataxia that is explained by weakness or paralysis.
Using UN for reasons the instrument does not allow (only amputation or joint fusion for limbs; intubation or physical barrier for dysarthria).
Scoring a pre-existing deficit as new without documenting it.

guideSections.what: A 15-item examination that quantifies selected neurological deficits after stroke. Totals range 0–42.
guideSections.whenToUse: Initial assessment of suspected stroke, serial monitoring for change, communication between teams, and research outcomes.
guideSections.howToPerform: Administer the items in the listed order and record each score immediately. Do not go back and change scores. Score what the patient does, not what you think they can do. Do not coach unless an item allows it. Use UN only where the instrument allows it, and record the reason.
guideSections.clinicalContext: The NIHSS supports, but does not replace, the full neurological examination and imaging. Treatment decisions combine it with timing, imaging, patient factors and local protocol.
